newsitem.title: USA: Stocks soar on weak CPI data.
newsitem.headline: Stocks soar on weak CPI data.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average surged early Friday, jumping through the record closing high reached in mid-May after the government reported more proof that inflation is well under control, which eased worries over an interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve.
AT 9:45 a.m. EDT, the Dow was up 42.17 points at 5,814.11, eclipsing its closing high of 5,778.00 set on May 22.
The Labour Department said the Consumer Price Index rose 0.1 percent last month, following an increase of 0.3 percent in July. Food prices rose, while energy and apparel prices fell.
The inflation-sensitive Treasury bond market surged, with the benchmark 30-year bond soaring more than a full point, pulling its yield down to 6.97 percent from Thursday's 7.08 percent.

"(Falling below 7 percent) tells me the bond market thinks inflation is under control, for the near- to intermediate-term and bond investors are anticipating the Fed will not raise rates in September," said Sam Stovall, strategist at Standard & Poor's.
There had been concern recently that a pick-up in inflation would prompt the Federal Reserve's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee to raise short-term interest rates at its Sept. 24 meeting.
"Goldilocks is back -- the economy is not too hot or too cold," said David Shulman, chief equity strategist at Salomon Brothers.

"Looking at the T-bill curve, the market consensus is there will be no tightening. Stocks are going straight up today. This is the kind of environment where we'll have a Dow 6000 by the election," he said.
Evidence that inflation was still in check has been accumulating this week. On Thursday, the Labour Department reported that wholesale prices rose moderately last month.

The Producer Price Index edged up 0.3 percent last month, after showing no change in July. The more closely watched "core" PPI, which factors out volatile food and energy costs, fell 0.1 percent after rising 0.1 percent in July.
Wall Street was in a buying mood as the Dow romped into record territory.
"September had not been expected to give much movement, but for now it looks like it's up, up and away. Records are made to be broken," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
